result.verdict: The second M2 assembly (9b02f05) passes the hard gates I checked. Arcade goldens were 20/20 and 17/17 identical. No frozen file was touched. F1–F3 and F7 and the path check are green. The new structures (canopy, bridges, city houses, gates, border) caused no new occlusion of cars in my probe at 13 places. Instance uniforms stayed at or below 141 of 230. Memory showed no leak over 15 min and over 215 km (all measured). However, I found one new high-severity picture defect that the assembly did not report. After a tunnel exit by day, Modern washes the whole picture out for about 1 s (snow: 65–68 % pure white against Arcade's 0.3 %; dry: 15–19 % against 1–3 %), and before that it shows 3 frames of brown, snow-free landscape. While the picture is washed out, the lane markings are barely visible (Rule 9). Modern is clearly better than Arcade in the Nürnberg old town, at structures, and in wet or snowy night scenes. On the open motorway (S1, S3, Deck) it only looks the same, so the user's wish for a 'deutliche Überarbeitung' is not met there. Several things look worse than Arcade: foreground and bend-side vegetation is missing, the city houses in Hamburg have fewer lit windows at night than Arcade and than the base, the fuel-station canopy is darker at night (0.77×), and the player cars' paint is too light at night. On performance, every counter is inside its budget. 'Hoch' casts 3.4× the shadow primitives of the base, and render() takes 2.5–2.9 ms against the 1.5 ms budget (the base already needed 2.1–2.3 ms). The single-frame hitches sit at the same places as in the base but are 2–3× heavier; at night the largest ones (64–159 ms) did not come back in a repeat run. The VM ran at load 8–14 during the whole check, so everything about real hardware or the Steam Deck is inferred, not measured. I would not ship the tunnel-exit whiteout (F-01) in the next test build; everything else can go in.

findings.where: scripts/race3d/layers/lights.gd add_reflectors() Z.238-243, _update_glints() Z.562-565; trigger chunk_streamer.gd _commit_step()/_drop()/_make_room()/clear(), builders/roadside.gd Z.395-399
findings.problem: Since B-01 a chunk can be dropped while it is COMMITTING (it never entered the tree), for example through _make_room() with max_chunks full or through clear(). roadside.commit() has already called lights.add_reflectors(mi, list) by then. The lights layer forgets reflectors only on tree_exiting, which never comes for such a node. After _free_trash() frees it, every _update_glints() with the low beam on raises SCRIPT ERROR and aborts, so the reflector glints freeze for the rest of the stage. FIX-RINT guarded _statics and the flares with is_instance_valid, but not _reflectors.
findings.evidence: measured: probe m1/NACH-RINT/sh/probe_reflectors.gd with the real lights.gd. Register a reflector on an out-of-tree node, free the node, call _update_glints 3x -> 3x 'SCRIPT ERROR: Trying to assign invalid previously freed instance. at: _update_glints (lights.gd:563)', and _reflector_count stays 1. Not observed in 3 real threaded drives (KH day and night, Saragossa-Pau night; 0 errors). How often it happens in play is inferred: rarely.
findings.fix: In _update_glints() drop entries whose pair[0] is not is_instance_valid() and lower _reflector_count, as _update_pools() does for _statics; or let the streamer notify the layers when it drops a COMMITTING chunk. Add a unit test: reflector on a node that is never added, free it, update the glints -> no error and a count of 0.
